canDo: Can tell apart something just finished, background, completed events and “the past before the past”, turning an experience into a clear timeline.
review: Review passé composé / imparfait; learn the passé récent and plus-que-parfait to build a four-layer past timeline.
input: Listening and reading about travel experiences, paying attention to the order of the story.
output: Write 140 words about a trip; retell it aloud in 3 minutes and answer follow-up questions.
checkpoint: Correctly distinguish passé composé / imparfait in a story, and understand or actively use the passé récent and plus-que-parfait.
challenge: Today’s challenge: in RFI’s Journal en français facile, find a news item about travel or a transport breakdown and retell it in 4 sentences, including one with venir de + infinitive and one in the plus-que-parfait (Les voyageurs avaient déjà…); then write one sentence comparing it with a trip of your own.

questions.why: The forecast deterioration was for the next evening, and they set off on time. The mistake was adding a secondary summit on the spot “because there was time”.
« plutôt que de continuer vers le refuge, pourtant plus proche » — which is why it seemed absurd at the time.
« La leçon n'est pas « il faut avoir un guide ». Elle est plus simple… » The author explicitly rules out “you need a guide”.
« ce n'est pas le train qui crée ces moments : c'est l'absence d'alternative », and he says plainly that he doesn’t wish for breakdowns.
She shared with two French people and spoke English to customers at the café. The breakthrough only came after she changed flatshare in January.
« Ils s'étaient renseignés … mais sur l'horaire de la marée d'un port situé à trente kilomètres », about an hour and a half different locally.
« La ville en compte deux qui portent presque le même nom ». All the pupils were there.
« les élèves étaient tous là, on a marché » — one kilometre, twenty minutes.
On the second day they couldn’t set off at all, because Marion’s knee hurt.
« Montrez-nous d'abord ce que votre outil fait de plus » — polite but firm.
